outcomes.text: Talk and write about relationships with family and friends, and about marriage and partnership.
Give information and opinions on family life in Hebrew.
Understand spoken and written texts on family, friends and partnership.
Discuss social media and mobile technology, with opinions and reasons.
Discuss music, cinema and TV, food and eating out, and sport.
Describe customs and festivals in Hebrew-speaking communities.

topics.title: 3.1.2 Theme 2: Local, national, international and global areas of interest

outcomes.text: Describe home, town, neighbourhood and region.
Understand and give directions and descriptions of places.
Discuss charity and voluntary work.
Discuss healthy and unhealthy living.
Discuss the environment, poverty and homelessness.
Discuss travel and tourism, including holidays and travel arrangements.

topics.title: 3.1.3 Theme 3: Current and future study and employment

outcomes.text: Talk and write about school subjects and studies.
Give opinions on subjects with reasons.
Describe daily life at school or college.
Discuss plans for education after age 16.
Discuss jobs, career choices and ambitions.
Show general and specific understanding of clear standard spoken Hebrew in the specified contexts.
Identify the message, key points, details and opinions in short and longer passages, recognising past, present and future.
Deduce meaning from longer texts, including narratives and authentic material on contemporary and cultural themes.
Answer questions, extract information, evaluate and draw conclusions from extended spoken texts.
Hold a short conversation, asking and answering questions and exchanging opinions.
Convey information and narrate events coherently, adapting language for new purposes.
Speak spontaneously, using rephrasing and repair to keep communication going.
Develop conversations with extended speech and varied vocabulary and structures across past, present and future.
Express and justify thoughts creatively, with accurate pronunciation and intonation.
Understand general and specific details in written texts, including authentic sources and adapted literary extracts.
Identify message, key points and opinions in short and longer texts across past, present and future.
Scan for information, draw inferences and recognise implicit meaning.
Translate a short passage from Hebrew into English.
Write short texts with simple sentences and familiar language to convey meaning.
Write extended coherent text to present facts, ideas and opinions for different purposes.
Use varied vocabulary and structures to describe and narrate across past, present and future, adapting style and register.
Translate sentences and short texts from English into Hebrew accurately.
Apply grammar knowledge at the right tier, treating marked structures as receptive only.
Use correct masculine and feminine forms, especially in numerals, and correct prepositions and pronunciation.
Identify noun gender, including feminine endings and feminine-by-nature nouns.
Use dual forms such as eyes, hands, trousers and two weeks.
Form masculine and feminine plurals, including irregular ones.
Express possession with the word "of" or pronominal suffixes, including vowel-changing nouns and segolites.
Use the construct state with unchanged and changed forms.
Conjugate sound verbs in the Qal, Nif'al, Pi'el, Hitpa'el and Hif'il of common verbs.
Use prefixes, infixes and suffixes and conjugate weak verbs, with a selection of useful verbs.
Use common adjectives with plural endings and agreement.
Form positive, comparative and superlative.
Use common adverbs according to their syntactic function.
Use personal, possessive, demonstrative and relative pronouns and the object particle.
Use the article with nouns and adjectives.
Recognise declined prepositions and use common prepositions, conjunctions and question words.
Use condition, negation, reason, contrast, indefinite and interjection words, and intonation questions.
Use cardinal numbers masculine and feminine, ordinals 1 to 10, dates and time.
Build simple and basic complex sentences with subject, verb, object, adverbs and attributes.
Use basic word order, noun and adjective order, and possession such as "I have time".
Apply all Foundation grammar plus the Higher Tier additions.
Use the Pu'al and Hof'al forms and consonant changes in the Hitpa'el.
Use quadriliteral verbs in the Pi'el, Pu'al and Hitpa'el.
Use declined prepositions actively and more particles, including prepositions with interrogatives.
Use conjunctions and phrases such as "although", "because of", "still not" and "therefore".
Use composite numbers and 10,000 to 1,000,000.
Use the infinitive as an impersonal subject, as in "it is necessary" or "it is forbidden".
Use communication strategies to cope with unknown words when listening, reading, speaking and writing.
Use layout, title and verbal context to guess meaning.
Infer new word meanings from the sentence around them.
Ignore unneeded words, since key points are often repeated.
Use pictures, film, sound, mime and gestures to understand and memorise words.
Use intonation and punctuation such as question and exclamation marks.
Infer unknown words from familiar roots and derivatives.
Use prefixes and suffixes: article, "and", prepositions, future tense, relative "that", feminine, dual and plural.
Use noun and verb patterns that mark places, tools, professions, illnesses and colours.
Use shared social, economic, legal, political and sporting concepts and slang borrowed from English.
Recognise cognates, and Hebrew words used in English such as Shalom and Mazal Tov.
Use these strategies to get meaning across despite an imperfect command of the language.
Use gesture, mime, expression, intonation and drawing.
Use synonyms, words from a related field, or similar items for a forgotten word.
Ask for help in Hebrew and use simpler forms without overusing them.
Use intonation, paraphrase and reference to features of an item, and avoid topic avoidance.
Use the minimum core vocabulary lists to plan learning, transferring words across themes.
Understand the rubrics and instructions used in listening and reading exam sections.
Learn general vocabulary that works across all themes.
Learn words for comparisons.
Learn conjunctions.
Learn connectives.
Learn prepositions.
Learn negatives.
Learn the Hebrew alphabet.
Learn numbers.
Learn words about money.
Learn question words.
Learn greetings and exclamations.
Learn words for giving opinions.
Learn the seasons.
Learn the months of the year.
Tell the time using the clock.
Learn other expressions of time.
Learn words for location and distance.
Learn weights and measures.
Learn words for shapes.
Learn weather vocabulary.
Learn words about access.
Learn words for correctness.
Learn words for materials.
Learn common abbreviations.
Learn the core Foundation vocabulary for each theme.
Learn Foundation words for identity and culture.
Learn Foundation words for local, national, international and global areas.
Learn Foundation words for current and future study and employment.
Learn the extra Higher Tier vocabulary for each theme.
Learn Higher words for identity and culture.
Learn Higher words for local, national, international and global areas.
Learn Higher words for current and future study and employment.
